  • Provide practical HR advice and support across the full employee lifecycle

job.title: People Manager
job.description:
An opportunity has emerged for an experienced People Manager to join a highly regarded organisation where the People function plays an important role in shaping both the employee experience and broader business strategy.

This is a role for someone who enjoys being close to the business. You’ll partner with senior stakeholders, bringing sound judgement, commercial thinking and the confidence to navigate complex people matters, while also looking ahead at how the organisation can continue to evolve.

You’ll work across talent, capability, engagement, employee relations, workforce planning and broader people initiatives, with the opportunity to influence how the People agenda comes to life.

The opportunity
Working closely with senior leaders and colleagues across the People function, you will:
  • Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, providing pragmatic and commercially considered people advice.
  • Coach leaders to build sustainable, high-performing teams, with a strong focus on talent, engagement and retention.
  • Navigate complex employee relations, performance and grievance matters with confidence and sound judgement.
  • Contribute to strategic People projects and initiatives spanning employee experience, talent, resourcing, capability and development.
  • Support workforce and resource planning, helping the business think proactively about capability and mobility.
  • Oversee key People processes and ensure they are delivered to a consistently high standard.
  • Work collaboratively across specialist People teams to create a connected employee experience.
  • Bring curiosity and fresh thinking to process improvement, including how AI can enhance the way the People function operates.
About you
You’ll be an experienced HR generalist who is comfortable operating in a complex, partnership model environment. Just as importantly, you’ll know how to build credibility quickly and balance the needs of your stakeholders with what is right for the broader organisation.

  • Strong employee relations capability, including complex performance matters
  • Significant experience as a Senior HR Business Partner
  • Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills.
  • Commercial acumen and an ability to connect People decisions with broader strategic priorities.
  • Confidence working autonomously through ambiguity and change.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Genuine curiosity about better ways of working, including the role AI can play within contemporary People functions.
Why this role?

What makes this opportunity particularly appealing is the combination of strategic exposure and genuine hands on partnering. You’ll operate with a high degree of autonomy, work closely with senior stakeholders and have the opportunity to influence both immediate people outcomes and longer-term organisational priorities. It would suit someone who is commercially minded, naturally curious and comfortable challenging thinking but who also understands that great HR is ultimately built on relationships, judgement and trust.
 
If you are confident that your experience reflects the above criteria, please apply online quoting ref No.4089460. Should you have any questions please contact Clare Johnston at clare@tandempartners.com.au

job.title: Senior Advisor - Workplace Relations
job.description:
Full job description 

Opportunity to join a large, complex and evolving organisation with a significant multi-site footprint across Australia. Experiencing a period of growth and organisational change, the business is continuing to mature the way its People function delivers specialist support and capability to its leaders.

A dedicated workplace relations function has recently been established. Working closely with the National Workplace Relations Lead, the Senior Workplace Relations Advisor will play an important role in both delivering high-quality workplace relations support and helping shape how the function operates into the future.

This is a hands-on role encompassing the full spectrum of workplace relations, including complex case management, investigations, performance and conduct matters, fitness for work, industrial instrument interpretation, union engagement and Fair Work Commission matters. The position will provide practical workplace relations advice to leaders and People teams, balancing legislative requirements, commercial and operational considerations, risk and employee outcomes.

You will also have the opportunity to influence workplace relations frameworks, policies and processes and build greater capability amongst leaders and the broader People function.

Key responsibilities
  • Manage complex employee and workplace relations matters end-to-end, including misconduct, performance management, grievances, workplace investigations, disciplinary processes and fitness for work matters.
  • Provide pragmatic and technically sound advice on the Fair Work Act, National Employment Standards, modern awards, enterprise agreements, employment contracts and other relevant employment legislation.
  • Partner with leaders to assess workplace relations risk and develop practical, lawful and human-centred solutions.
  • Prepare submissions and represent the organisation in matters before the Fair Work Commission and other relevant tribunals.
  • Coach and guide leaders through workplace relations matters, building their confidence and capability to manage issues effectively and consistently.
  • Draft, review and enhance workplace relations policies, procedures, guidance materials and employment documentation.
  • Identify emerging and systemic workplace relations issues and recommend improvements to processes and ways of working.
  • Interpret enterprise agreements and industrial instruments and contribute to broader industrial relations activity, including union engagement and industrial disputes.
About you
  • Previous experience operating within a large, complex and multi-site environment.
  • Strong knowledge of the Fair Work Act, National Employment Standards, modern awards, enterprise agreements and Australian employment legislation.
  • Experience operating across multiple Australian jurisdictions and providing workplace relations support at scale.
  • Demonstrated experience independently managing complex investigations, performance, conduct and broader employee relations matters.
  • Experience preparing submissions and responding to matters before the Fair Work Commission, including conciliation.
  • Exposure to unionised environments and industrial instruments, with experience supporting enterprise bargaining or broader industrial relations activity advantageous.
  • Experience within healthcare, critical services or other complex and highly regulated operating environments will be highly regarded.
  • Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to establish credibility with stakeholders ranging from frontline leaders through to executives.
  • A pragmatic and commercial approach, with the judgement to assess risk.
  • A collaborative and human-centred style, with the resilience to navigate challenging conversations and competing stakeholder perspectives.
  • The confidence to work autonomously in a fast-paced environment while remaining curious, adaptable and open to new ways of working.
  • Strong written communication, negotiation, conflict resolution and analytical skills.
If you are confident that your experience reflects the above criteria, please apply online quoting ref No.4088854. Should you have any questions please contact Georgina Norman at georgina@tandempartners.com.au

  • Develop program communications and maintain learning content and resources across SharePoint
  • Support learning technology, including LMS administration, system upgrades, testing and user documentation
  • Contribute to leadership, technical capability and
  • Assist with learning reports and mandatory training dashboards
    AI learning initiatives across the organisation
The role also involves working with global colleagues, including fortnightly scheduled calls outside standard business hours.

You are proactive, organised and comfortable taking responsibility for the detail. You will ideally bring:

job.title: L&OD Specialist

  • Proven success delivering organisation-wide change, capability or people initiatives from concept through to implementation.
